_meta.name: National Early Warning Score (NEWS) 2 — scoring bands and triggers
_meta.source: Royal College of Physicians. National Early Warning Score (NEWS) 2: Standardising the assessment of acute-illness severity in the NHS. Updated report of a working party. London: RCP, 2017.

_meta.generatedBy: Transcribed from the RCP chart with AI assistance (Claude). Must be checked by a human against the source chart before use.
_meta.notes: All ranges are inclusive. Temperature in °C, blood pressure is systolic in mmHg, pulse in beats/min, respiration in breaths/min, SpO2 in %.

spo2Scale2._use: Only when the target range is 88-92% (e.g. hypercapnic respiratory failure) and under the direction of a qualified clinician. Otherwise use Scale 1.

triggers.rule: score of 3 in any individual parameter

limits: Do not use in people under 16 or in pregnancy.
May be unreliable with spinal cord injury (tetraplegia or high-level paraplegia).
An aid to clinical assessment, not a substitute for clinical judgement; concern about the patient overrides the score.
Suspected infection with a score of 5 or more: think sepsis.
If confusion may be new, assume it is new until confirmed otherwise.
If a parameter cannot be measured for lack of equipment, calculate the score anyway and mark it incomplete.
NEWS2 is validated for hospital and prehospital care on Earth, not for spaceflight.
